div.head: Geþyncðo Inscr.
div.ab: On the Ranks of People and Law
Von des Volkes Würden und Berechtigung (Von Wergeldern und von Würden. D)
Of the people's ranks and law (Of wergilds and of ranks. D)
div.note: Liebermann prints D (Cambridge, Corpus Christi College 201, p. 101, after the Canons of Edgar, c. 1060) and H (Textus Roffensis f. 93, after VI As, same hand, c. 1120), with the Quadripartitus and the Instituta Cnuti III 60–63.1. K is H; D is also given here. H's heading is in red; D's is probably not original (perhaps referring to Norðleod and Mirce). Liebermann notes that Geþyncðo, Norðleod, Mirce, Að and Had stand only in MSS going back to one archetype before c. 1060, which held them in this order; they show traces of composition after 1027, perhaps by one hand, and Geþyncðo may be meant as an introduction to the next two pieces. He dates Geþyncðo c. 1029–c. 1060. The language is in places raised by rhythm and alliteration. Clause number standardised from ‘Geþyncðo Inscr.’.

Manuscripts: O = Cambridge, Corpus Christi College MS 190, pp. 418–20; D = Cambridge, Corpus Christi College MS 201, pp. 101–3; H = Strood, Medway Archive and Local Studies Centre MS DRc/R1 (Textus Roffensis), fols. 7r–v, 39v, 93r–v, 93v–94r. Be . . . lage: Be wergildum and be geðinðum D

The text here is based on that in Textus Roffensis, though Wulfstan’s original order has been preserved. Significant variants from Cambridge, Corpus Christi College MSS 190 and 201 have been identified in the notes.
